question: If a motor car travels the first half of a distance at a speed of 30 km/h and the remaining half distance at a speed of 50 km/h, what will be its average speed?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = (2xy) ÷ (x + y)

Here, x = 30 km/h and y = 50 km/h.

Average Speed = (2 × 30 × 50) ÷ (30 + 50)

Average Speed = 3000 ÷ 80 = 37.5 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 37.5 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed for the first half of the distance = 30 km/h

Speed for the remaining half of the distance = 50 km/h

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 Distance = d
 Speed = 30 km/h
 
 Distance = d
 Speed = 50 km/h

 Total Distance = 2d

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the distance of each half be d km.

⇒ Total Distance = d + d = 2d km.

⇒ Time taken for the first half = d ÷ 30 hours.

⇒ Time taken for the second half = d ÷ 50 hours.

⇒ Total Time = (d ÷ 30) + (d ÷ 50)

⇒ Total Time = (5d + 3d) ÷ 150 = 8d ÷ 150 = 4d ÷ 75 hours.

⇒ Average Speed = 2d ÷ (4d ÷ 75)

⇒ Average Speed = (2d × 75) ÷ 4d = 150 ÷ 4 = 37.5 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 37.5 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

If a person covers three equal distances at speeds x, y, and z, the Average Speed = (3xyz) ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Average Speed for Different Distances

When distances and speeds are completely different, you must find the total time taken for all individual parts and use the base formula: Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time) = (d₁ + d₂ + ...) ÷ (t₁ + t₂ + ...).

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in the same direction, Relative Speed = Difference in their speeds (x − y). When moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = Sum of their speeds (x + y).
